name: Elizabeth I
description: Queen of England whose 45-year reign steadied a religiously divided realm, saw off the Spanish Armada (1588), and presided over a flowering of English drama and seafaring — while she mastered the politics of an unmarried female sovereign in a dynastic age.

name: Galileo Galilei
description: Pisan mathematician who turned the new telescope on the heavens — finding Jupiter's moons, Venus's phases, and lunar mountains — and championed Copernicanism until the Inquisition forced his abjuration. His kinematics laid groundwork for Newton.

name: Isaac Newton
description: English mathematician whose Principia (1687) unified terrestrial and celestial mechanics under three laws of motion and universal gravitation, and who co-invented calculus — establishing the mathematical framework of physics for two centuries.

name: Peter the Great
description: Russian tsar who dragged his realm toward European technology and administration — building a navy from nothing, defeating Sweden in the Great Northern War, and raising a new capital, Saint Petersburg, on the Baltic marshes.

name: Benjamin Franklin
description: Printer, scientist, and statesman: proved lightning electrical, invented the lightning rod and bifocals, edited the Declaration of Independence, and negotiated the French alliance and the peace that secured American independence.
